## Unique Differentially expressed genes by grouping them into unique subsets per contrast
Unique DEGs lists from ggvenn intersections, adding log2 fold changes and other columns from de_results_list

Generate a new list where each subset is extracted from de_results_list based on the item column from degs_ggvenn_list, while keeping the same format as de_results_list and
adding the id and name columns from degs_ggvenn_list
Iterates through degs_ggvenn_list, which contains the intersection details.
Extracts the name and item columns from each row.
Splits the item column into a vector of gene IDs.
Finds the corresponding dataset in de_results_list using name as a key.
Subsets de_results_list using the gene_id column to match genes from item.
Adds the id and name columns to the subsetted data.
Stores the subsetted data in degs_subset_list, ensuring unique names using both venn_name and id.

```{r uniquedegs}
# Create an empty list to store the unique subset results
degs_unique_list <- list()

# Iterate over each element in degs_ggvenn_list
for (venn_name in names(degs_ggvenn_list)) {
  venn_data <- degs_ggvenn_list[[venn_name]]
  
  # Iterate over each row in the tibble
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(venn_data))) {
    contrast_name <- venn_data$name[i]
    gene_ids <- unlist(strsplit(venn_data$item[i], ", "))  # Convert item column to gene vector
    
    # Check if the contrast_name exists in de_results_list
    if (contrast_name %in% names(de_results_list)) {
      # Subset based on gene_id
      subset_data <- de_results_list[[contrast_name]][de_results_list[[contrast_name]]$gene_id %in% gene_ids, ]
      
      # Add id and name columns
      subset_data$id <- venn_data$id[i]
      subset_data$name <- venn_data$name[i]
      
      # Store in the new list using a unique key
      key_name <- paste0(venn_name, "_", venn_data$id[i])
      degs_unique_list[[key_name]] <- subset_data
    }
  }
}

# Print structure of the new unique subset list
str(degs_unique_list)
print(names(degs_unique_list))
str(degs_unique_list[[1]])
head(degs_unique_list[[1]])

# Get unique values for id and name columns
unique(degs_unique_list[[1]]$id)  
unique(degs_unique_list[[1]]$name)
```

## Functional Enrichment Analysis
Modified from the Data Carpentry tutorial on RNAseq data analysis:
https://scienceparkstudygroup.github.io/rna-seq-lesson/05-descriptive-plots/index.html

One important goal is to gain a higher view and not only deal with individual genes but understand which pathways are involved in the response.

Once we obtain a list of genes, we have multiple analysis to perform to go beyond a simple list of genes:

* Annotating our list of genes with cross-databases identifiers and descriptions (Entrezid, Uniprot, KEGG, etc.).
* Performing Over-Representation Analysis (ORA) or Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) using R or webtools.
* Interpreting the results.

From: https://yulab-smu.top/biomedical-knowledge-mining-book/enrichment-overview.html#ora-algorithm

## Over Representation Analysis (ORA) vs. Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA)
Over Representation Analysis (ORA) (Boyle et al. 2004) is a widely used approach to determine whether known biological functions or processes are over-represented (= enriched) in an experimentally-derived gene list, e.g. a list of differentially expressed genes (DEGs).

A common approach to analyzing gene expression profiles is identifying differentially expressed genes that are deemed interesting. The ORA enrichment analysis is based on these differentially expressed genes. This approach will find genes where the difference is large and will fail where the difference is small, but evidenced in coordinated way in a set of related genes. Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA)(Subramanian et al. 2005) directly addresses this limitation. All genes can be used in GSEA; GSEA aggregates the per gene statistics across genes within a gene set, therefore making it possible to detect situations where all genes in a predefined set change in a small but coordinated way. This is important since it is likely that many relevant phenotypic differences are manifested by small but consistent changes in a set of genes.

## Over Representation Analysis (ORA)

### Differentially expressed gene lists

The differentially expressed genes for each comparison for all tissues (unique and shared) are stored in the degs_unique_list object. This object contains the unique DEGs for each comparison, with the id and name columns from degs_ggvenn_list.

Removing the ".v2.1" from the gene names because the gene names in the annotation file do not have the ".v2.1" at the end.

Remove the ".v2.1" suffix from the gene_id column in both de_results_list and degs_unique_list:
```{r diff_genes2}
# Function to remove ".v2.1" from gene_id column in a list of data frames
remove_version_suffix <- function(de_list) {
  lapply(de_list, function(df) {
    df$gene_id <- gsub("\\.v2\\.1$", "", df$gene_id)  # Remove ".v2.1" from gene_id column
    return(df)
  })
}

# Apply the function to de_results_list
de_results_list <- remove_version_suffix(de_results_list)

# Apply the function to degs_unique_list
degs_unique_list <- remove_version_suffix(degs_unique_list)

# Check the result
head(de_results_list[[1]])
head(degs_unique_list[[1]])

```


## Create separate lists for upregulated and downregulated genes

```{r updown}
# Initialize lists for upregulated and downregulated genes
de_upregulated_list <- list()
de_downregulated_list <- list()

# Loop through each contrast in de_results_list
for (contrast_name in names(de_results_list)) {
  dataset <- de_results_list[[contrast_name]]
  
  # Ensure log2FoldChange is numeric
  dataset$log2FoldChange <- as.numeric(dataset$log2FoldChange)
  
  # Filter upregulated genes (positive log2FC)
  upregulated_genes <- subset(dataset, log2FoldChange > 0)
  
  # Filter downregulated genes (negative log2FC)
  downregulated_genes <- subset(dataset, log2FoldChange < 0)
  
  # Save results in respective lists
  de_upregulated_list[[contrast_name]] <- upregulated_genes
  de_downregulated_list[[contrast_name]] <- downregulated_genes
  
  # Print summary
  cat("Processed:", contrast_name, "\n",
      "Upregulated:", nrow(upregulated_genes), "genes\n",
      "Downregulated:", nrow(downregulated_genes), "genes\n\n")
}

# Save results as RData for later use
save(de_upregulated_list, file = "2.FunctionalAnalysis/output/de_upregulated_genes.RData")
save(de_downregulated_list, file = "2.FunctionalAnalysis/output/de_downregulated_genes.RData")
load("2.FunctionalAnalysis/output/de_upregulated_genes.RData")
load("2.FunctionalAnalysis/output/de_downregulated_genes.RData")
```


These are the log fold changes for each comparison, to use later in Category Network plots, and sorting the genes in decreasing order of log fold change (required for clusterProfiler).

```{r log_folds}
# Function to extract, name, remove NAs, and sort log2 fold changes
extract_lfc_sorted <- function(de_list) {
  lfc_list <- lapply(de_list, function(df) {
    lfc <- df$log2FoldChange  # Extract log2 fold change
    names(lfc) <- df$gene_id  # Name the vector using gene IDs
    lfc <- na.omit(lfc)  # Remove NA values
    lfc <- sort(lfc, decreasing = TRUE)  # Sort in decreasing order
    return(lfc)
  })
  return(lfc_list)
}

# Extract log2 fold changes from de_results_list
lfc_de_results_list <- extract_lfc_sorted(de_results_list)
lfc_de_upregulated_list <- extract_lfc_sorted(de_upregulated_list)
lfc_de_downregulated_list <- extract_lfc_sorted(de_downregulated_list)

# Extract log2 fold changes from degs_unique_list
lfc_degs_unique_list <- extract_lfc_sorted(degs_unique_list)
lfc_degs_unique_list_pos <- extract_lfc_sorted(degs_unique_list_pos)


# Check results
head(lfc_de_results_list[[1]])
head(lfc_degs_unique_list[[1]])
```

### Fold changes for each dataset (positive, above 75th percentile, negative, and below 25th percentile)

Loop through all datasets of differentially expressed genes. For each dataset, create a list of genes with positive fold changes, fold changes above the 75th percentile, negative fold changes, and fold changes below the 25th percentile. Write each list of genes to a file.

This code assigns each filtered dataset (positive, above 75th percentile, negative, and below 25th percentile) as a separate R object with specific names. 

We converted downregulated values to positive values because our reference is not a control. Instead, we aim to interpret differential expression in terms of upregulation in both the target and reference groups.

For example, in the comparison Red Hawk vs. Stampede (Rh vs. St), where Red Hawk is the reference, the interpretation is as follows:

Positive log₂FoldChange values indicate genes upregulated in Stampede relative to Red Hawk.
Negative log₂FoldChange values (converted to positive) indicate genes upregulated in Red Hawk relative to Stampede.
By transforming negative fold changes into positive values, we enable a uniform interpretation of upregulated genes across both groups, facilitating biological insights into differential gene expression patterns.

```{r dedatasets}
# Function to filter log2 fold changes above the 75th percentile (upregulated) 
# and below the 25th percentile (downregulated, converted to positive values)
filter_lfc_thresholds <- function(lfc_list, output_dir, dataset_name_prefix) {
  # Ensure the output directory exists
  if (!dir.exists(output_dir)) dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE)

  # Initialize lists to store filtered genes
  upregulated_list <- list()
  downregulated_list <- list()

  for (contrast_name in names(lfc_list)) {
    lfc_vector <- lfc_list[[contrast_name]]
    
    # Compute the 75th and 25th percentile cutoffs
    q_75 <- quantile(lfc_vector, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
    q_25 <- quantile(lfc_vector, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE)
    
    # Extract upregulated genes (above 75th percentile)
    upregulated_genes <- names(lfc_vector[lfc_vector > q_75])
    upregulated_list[[contrast_name]] <- upregulated_genes
    
    # Save upregulated genes to file
    write.table(upregulated_genes, 
                file = paste0(output_dir, "/", dataset_name_prefix, "_upregulated_", contrast_name, ".tsv"),
                row.names = FALSE, col.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)
    
    # Extract downregulated genes (below 25th percentile, and convert to positive values)
    downregulated_genes <- names(lfc_vector[lfc_vector < q_25])
    downregulated_values <- abs(lfc_vector[lfc_vector < q_25])  # Convert to positive values
    downregulated_list[[contrast_name]] <- downregulated_genes
    
    # Save downregulated genes to file
    write.table(downregulated_genes, 
                file = paste0(output_dir, "/", dataset_name_prefix, "_downregulated_", contrast_name, ".tsv"),
                row.names = FALSE, col.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)
  }
  
  return(list(upregulated = upregulated_list, downregulated = downregulated_list))
}

# Define output directories
output_dir_results <- "2.FunctionalAnalysis/output/lfc_de_results"
output_dir_unique <- "2.FunctionalAnalysis/output/lfc_degs_unique"

# Apply function to both lfc_de_results_list and lfc_degs_unique_list
lfc_results_filtered <- filter_lfc_thresholds(lfc_de_results_list, output_dir_results, "de_results")
lfc_unique_filtered <- filter_lfc_thresholds(lfc_degs_unique_list, output_dir_unique, "degs_unique")

# Check the results

head(lfc_results_filtered$downregulated[[1]])
names(lfc_results_filtered$upregulated)

str(lfc_unique_filtered)
```

## Convert All Log₂ Fold Changes to Absolute Values
```{r}
# Function to convert all log2FoldChange values to positive
convert_to_positive <- function(de_list) {
  de_list_converted <- lapply(de_list, function(df) {
    if (!"log2FoldChange" %in% colnames(df)) {
      return(df)  # Skip if no log2FoldChange column
    }
    # Convert all log2 fold changes to absolute values (positive)
    df$log2FoldChange <- abs(df$log2FoldChange)
    
    return(df)
  })
  return(de_list_converted)
}

# Apply the function to both lists
de_downregulated_list_pos <- convert_to_positive(de_downregulated_list)
degs_unique_list_pos <- convert_to_positive(degs_unique_list)

de_results_list_pos <- convert_to_positive(de_results_list) #this is converting together up and downregulated genes, so log2FoldChange can be used but de_resuls_list is not used in the following steps

lfc_de_results_list_pos <- extract_lfc_sorted(de_results_list_pos)
```

Create subsets of both de_results_list_pos and degs_unique_list_pos that include only those genes with a log₂ fold change above the 75th percentile for each contrast:

```{r}
# Function to subset genes with log2FoldChange above the 75th percentile
filter_above_75 <- function(de_list) {
  lapply(de_list, function(df) {
    # Calculate the 75th percentile cutoff for log2FoldChange
    cutoff <- quantile(df$log2FoldChange, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
    # Subset the data frame to keep only genes above the cutoff
    df_subset <- df[df$log2FoldChange > cutoff, ]
    return(df_subset)
  })
}

#Define a function to filter by abs(log2FoldChange) > 2
# Function to subset genes with absolute log2FC > 2
filter_abs_lfc_gt2 <- function(de_list) {
  lapply(de_list, function(df) {
    df_subset <- df[abs(df$log2FoldChange) > 2, ]
    return(df_subset)
  })
}

# Apply the functions to both lists
de_upregulated_list_75 <- filter_above_75(de_upregulated_list)
de_downregulated_list_75 <- filter_above_75(de_downregulated_list_pos)
degs_unique_list_75 <- filter_above_75(degs_unique_list_pos)

de_upregulated_list_lfc2 <- filter_abs_lfc_gt2(de_upregulated_list)
de_downregulated_list_lfc2 <- filter_abs_lfc_gt2(de_downregulated_list_pos)
degs_unique_list_lfc2 <- filter_abs_lfc_gt2(degs_unique_list_pos)
```

## GO id to GO ontology

add the ontology column to all_pv_genes_ann, and can split it for enricher()
```{r}

  filter(go_id != "") %>%

# Step 3: Merge ontology info back into *full* annotation table

  left_join(go_ontology_map, by = c("go_id" = "GOID"))
```

### Retrieving GO annotations for the differentially expressed genes for each contrast
Getting the annotation for the differentially expressed genes for each contrast.
We are retrieving the organism name, gene name, gene id, go id, and go description.


### Using DE genes separately (upregulated, upregulated top 75th percentile, downregulated (converted to positive), and downregulated (converted to positive) top 75th percentile)

For each contrast (dataset), we have:
- upregulated genes
- upregulated genes above the 75th percentile
- downregulated genes (converted to positive values)
- downregulated genes above the 75th percentile

The interpreation is as follows: 
- Positive log₂FoldChange values indicate genes upregulated in the target group relative to the reference group.
- Negative log₂FoldChange values (converted to positive (absolute)) indicate genes upregulated in the reference group relative to the target group.

Contrast names and reference and target groups are specified in contrasts_df (the original file in: (contrasts_df <- read.csv("Results_nf_pipelines/ResultsDiffExp_nfcore_Repblock_onlyroots_shiny/tables/contrast/contrasts_pairwise_TissueDayGenotype_Rep_onlyroots.csv")
)).

Annotating genes in each contrast within de_results_list_pos, degs_unique_list_pos, de_results_list_75, and degs_unique_list_75. It follows these steps:

- Query and store full annotations with all relevant attributes.
- Save the full annotation dataset for future flexibility.
- Extract GO/KEGG annotations separately for functional enrichment analysis.

Separately processes and annotates genes for each of the lists:

- de_upregulated_list
- de_downregulated_list
- de_upregulated_list_75
- de_downregulated_list_75
- degs_unique_list_pos
- degs_unique_list_75

# Annotate only de_results_list_75[[2]] using both full and GO/KEGG-only attributes:
```{r}
# Load required libraries
library(biomaRt)
library(dplyr)

# Define annotation attributes
attributes_full <- c("organism_name", "gene_name1", "gene_description", 
                     "go_id", "go_desc", "kegg_id", "kegg_desc", 
                     "pathway_id", "pathway_desc", 
                     "pfam_id", "pfam_desc", 
                     "interpro_id", "interpro_desc")

attributes_go_kegg <- c("organism_name", "gene_name1", "gene_description", "gene_id", 
                        "go_id", "go_desc", "kegg_id", "kegg_desc")

attributes_go_kegg_path <- c("organism_name", "gene_name1", "gene_description", "gene_id", 
                            "go_id", "go_desc", "kegg_id", "kegg_desc", "pathway_desc")

# Extract the second contrast from de_results_list_75
contrast_name <- names(de_results_list_75)[2]
dataset <- de_results_list_75[[2]]

# Ensure there are genes to annotate
if (nrow(dataset) > 0) {
  
  # Full annotation
  annotated_full <- getBM(
    attributes = attributes_full, 
    filters = "gene_name_filter", 
    values = dataset$gene_id, 
    mart = phytozome_v13
  )

  
  # Save full annotation
  saveRDS(annotated_full, paste0("2.FunctionalAnalysis/output/annotated_", contrast_name, "_full.rds"))
  
  # GO & KEGG annotation
  annotated_go_kegg <- getBM(
    attributes = attributes_go_kegg, 
    filters = "gene_name_filter", 
    values = dataset$gene_id, 
    mart = phytozome_v13
  )
  
  # Merge GO/KEGG annotations with the original dataset
  annotated_de_results_75_go_kegg <- merge(dataset, annotated_go_kegg, by = "gene_id", all.x = TRUE)
  
  # Save GO/KEGG annotation
  saveRDS(annotated_de_results_75_go_kegg, paste0("2.FunctionalAnalysis/output/annotated_", contrast_name, "_go_kegg.rds"))

  # Print completion message
  print(paste("Annotation completed for contrast:", contrast_name))
  
} else {
  print(paste("No genes to annotate for contrast:", contrast_name))
}
```

Loop through each dataset, retrieve annotations using the specified filters and mart, and store the results in separate lists.

- de_upregulated_list
- de_downregulated_list
- de_upregulated_list_75
- de_downregulated_list_75
- degs_unique_list_pos
- degs_unique_list_75
- de_upregulated_list_lfc2
- de_downregulated_list_lfc2
- degs_unique_list_lfc2



# DEGs annotation only go
```{r}
attributes_go <- c("organism_name", "gene_name1", "gene_id", "go_id", "go_desc")

# Initialize empty lists to store annotated data
annotated_degs_unique <- list()
annotated_de_results_75 <- list()
annotated_de_results_pos <- list()
annotated_de_upregulated <- list()
annotated_de_downregulated <- list()
annotated_de_upregulated_75 <- list()
annotated_de_downregulated_75 <- list()
# Initialize empty lists for log2 fold changes
annotated_degs_unique_lfc2 <- list()
annotated_de_upregulated_lfc2 <- list()
annotated_de_downregulated_lfc2 <- list()


# Function to annotate a dataset
annotate_genes <- function(gene_ids) {
  if (length(gene_ids) > 0) {
    # Retrieve gene annotations from Phytozome
    gene_annotations <- getBM(
      attributes = attributes_go,
      filters = "gene_name_filter",  # Use the specified filter
      values = gene_ids,
      mart = phytozome_v13  # Use the specified mart
    )
    return(gene_annotations)
  } else {
    message("No genes to annotate in this dataset.")
    return(NULL)
  }
}

# List of datasets to annotate
datasets_to_annotate <- list(
  "degs_unique_list_pos" = degs_unique_list_pos,
  "degs_unique_list_75" = degs_unique_list_75,
  "de_upregulated_list" = de_upregulated_list,
  "de_downregulated_list" = de_downregulated_list,
  "de_upregulated_list_75" = de_upregulated_list_75,
  "de_downregulated_list_75" = de_downregulated_list_75,
  "degs_unique_list_lfc2" = degs_unique_list_lfc2,  # NEW
  "de_upregulated_list_lfc2" = de_upregulated_list_lfc2,  # NEW
  "de_downregulated_list_lfc2" = de_downregulated_list_lfc2   # NEW 
)

# Corresponding lists to store annotations
annotated_lists <- list(
  "degs_unique_list_pos" = annotated_degs_unique,
  "degs_unique_list_75" = annotated_de_results_75,
  "de_upregulated_list" = annotated_de_upregulated,
  "de_downregulated_list" = annotated_de_downregulated,
  "de_upregulated_list_75" = annotated_de_upregulated_75,
  "de_downregulated_list_75" = annotated_de_downregulated_75,
  "degs_unique_list_lfc2" = annotated_degs_unique_lfc2,  # NEW
  "de_upregulated_list_lfc2" = annotated_de_upregulated_lfc2,  # NEW
  "de_downregulated_list_lfc2" = annotated_de_downregulated_lfc2   # NEW
)

# Loop through each dataset and annotate
for (dataset_name in names(datasets_to_annotate)) {
  dataset <- datasets_to_annotate[[dataset_name]]
  annotated_list <- list()  # Temporary storage for each dataset
  
  for (contrast_name in names(dataset)) {
    gene_ids <- as.character(dataset[[contrast_name]]$gene_id)
    annotated_list[[contrast_name]] <- annotate_genes(gene_ids)
    message("Annotation completed for: ", dataset_name, " -> ", contrast_name)
  }
  
  # Store annotated data in the corresponding list
  annotated_lists[[dataset_name]] <- annotated_list
}

# Save results
save(annotated_lists, file = "2.FunctionalAnalysis/output/annotated_gene_lists_lfc2.RData")
load("2.FunctionalAnalysis/output/annotated_gene_lists_lfc2.RData")

head(annotated_lists[[2]][[1]])
head(annotated_lists[[4]][[1]])
```

```{r}
# Ensure GO terms are correctly ordered as a factor
ora_UniqHYPd5UpRh@result$Description <- factor(ora_UniqHYPd5UpRh@result$Description, levels = ora_UniqHYPd5UpRh@result$Description)

# Step 2: Extract genes from ordered GO terms, ensuring correct order

  dplyr::select(Description, geneID) %>%

filtered_lfc <- lfc_degs_unique_list_pos[[7]][ordered_gene_list]

  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#cedfce", high = "#710b7e") +

#Genes ordered by GO term based on q-value or GeneRatio and ordered by log2FC within each GO term
# Step 1: Order GO terms (y-axis) by q-value (lowest q-value first)
ora_UniqHYPd5UpSt@result <- ora_UniqHYPd5UpSt@result[order(ora_UniqHYPd5UpSt$qvalue, decreasing = TRUE), ]  # Ensures most significant GO terms appear first
#by GeneRatio
ora_UniqHYPd5UpSt@result <- ora_UniqHYPd5UpSt@result[order(ora_UniqHYPd5UpSt$GeneRatio, decreasing = TRUE), ]  # Ensures most significant GO terms appear first


# Ensure GO terms are correctly ordered as a factor
ora_UniqHYPd5UpSt@result$Description <- factor(ora_UniqHYPd5UpSt@result$Description, levels = ora_UniqHYPd5UpSt@result$Description)

# Step 2: Extract genes from ordered GO terms, ensuring correct order
gene_df <- ora_UniqHYPd5UpSt@result %>%
  dplyr::select(Description, geneID) %>%
  separate_rows(geneID, sep = "/")  # Expand genes into individual rows

# Step 3: Merge with log2 fold change values & sort within each GO term
gene_df <- gene_df %>%
  left_join(data.frame(Gene = names(lfc_degs_unique_list_pos[[15]]),
                       log2FC = lfc_degs_unique_list_pos[[15]]), 
            by = c("geneID" = "Gene")) %>%
  arrange(Description, desc(log2FC))  # Sort by GO term, then by highest log2FC

# Step 4: Get final ordered gene list (ensuring only `geneID` genes are included)
ordered_gene_list <- unique(gene_df$geneID)  

# Step 5: Filter the fold-change values to include only these genes
filtered_lfc <- lfc_degs_unique_list_pos[[15]][ordered_gene_list]

# Step 6: Generate heatplot with correctly ordered GO terms and genes
heat_UniqHYPd5UpSt <- heatplot(ora_UniqHYPd5UpSt, foldChange = filtered_lfc) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#cedfce", high = "#710b7e") +
  scale_y_discrete(limits = levels(ora_UniqHYPd5UpSt@result$Description)) +  # Order GO terms
  scale_x_discrete(limits = ordered_gene_list)  # Order genes within GO term by log2FC

# Display the heatmap
heat_UniqHYPd5UpSt


pdf("2.FunctionalAnalysis/figures/heatplot_ora_UniqHYPd5UpSt_gratio_sm.pdf", width = 7, height = 2.5)
print(heat_UniqHYPd5UpSt)  # Print the plot inside the PDF
dev.off()  # Close the PDF device
```

Loops through all annotated lists, performs ORA (Overrepresentation Analysis) using enricher(), and generates both dot plots and heat plots. The plots are saved as PDFs in a specified folder, named using the list name and contrast name.

```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(clusterProfiler)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggplotify)

# Define output folder for figures
output_folder <- "2.FunctionalAnalysis/figures/ora_plots_pval0p05/"
dir.create(output_folder, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Loop through each annotated list
for (list_name in names(annotated_lists)) {
  annotated_data <- annotated_lists[[list_name]]
  
  for (contrast_name in names(annotated_data)) {
    test_genes_ann <- as.data.frame(annotated_data[[contrast_name]])
    
    # Skip if there are no genes
    if (nrow(test_genes_ann) == 0 || is.null(test_genes_ann$gene_name1)) {
      message("Skipping ORA for: ", list_name, " -> ", contrast_name, " (No genes available)")
      next
    }
    
    # Perform ORA using enricher()
    ora_test <- enricher(
      gene = test_genes_ann$gene_name1,
      universe = all_pv_genes_ann$gene_name1,
      TERM2GENE = all_pv_genes_ann[, c("go_desc", "gene_name1")],
      pAdjustMethod = "BH",
      pvalueCutoff = 0.05 # changed from 0.1 to 0.05
    )
    
    # Check if ORA returned valid results
    if (is.null(ora_test) || nrow(ora_test) == 0) {
      message("No significant enrichment for: ", list_name, " -> ", contrast_name)
      next
    }
    
    # Generate Dot Plot
    dot_plot <- dotplot(ora_test, showCategory = 20, title = paste("ORA:", contrast_name))
    
    # Save Dot Plot as PDF
    dotplot_pdf <- paste0(output_folder, "dotplot_", list_name, "_", contrast_name, ".pdf")
    pdf(dotplot_pdf, width = 6.5, height = 6)
    print(dot_plot)
    dev.off()
    
    # Generate Heat Plot
    heat_plot <- heatplot(ora_test, foldChange = lfc_de_results_list_pos[[contrast_name]]) +
      scale_fill_gradient(low = "#cedfce", high = "#710b7e")
    
    # Save Heat Plot as PDF
    heatplot_pdf <- paste0(output_folder, "heatplot_", list_name, "_", contrast_name, ".pdf")
    pdf(heatplot_pdf, width = 10, height = 2.5)
    print(heat_plot)
    dev.off()
    
    message("Saved ORA plots for: ", list_name, " -> ", contrast_name)
  }
}

message("All ORA plots saved successfully.")

```


Extract the top 5 enriched GO terms from each ora_test in annotated_lists and save the results as a CSV file:
```{r}
# Initialize an empty data frame to store results
enriched_go_results <- data.frame()

# Loop through each list in annotated_lists
for (list_name in names(annotated_lists)) {
  
  # Loop through each contrast in the list
  for (contrast_name in names(annotated_lists[[list_name]])) {
    
    # Get the annotated genes for the contrast
    test_genes_ann <- as.data.frame(annotated_lists[[list_name]][[contrast_name]])
    
    # Perform ORA
    ora_test <- enricher(
      gene = test_genes_ann$gene_name1, 
      universe = all_pv_genes_ann$gene_name1, 
      TERM2GENE = all_pv_genes_ann[, c("go_desc", "gene_name1")], 
      pAdjustMethod = "BH",
      pvalueCutoff = 0.1
    )
    
    # Check if enrichment results exist
    if (!is.null(ora_test) && nrow(as.data.frame(ora_test)) > 0) {
      
      # Convert ORA results to a data frame
      ora_df <- as.data.frame(ora_test)
      
      # Select top 5 enriched GO terms
      top_5_ora <- ora_df[order(ora_df$p.adjust), ][1:min(5, nrow(ora_df)), ]
      
      # Add columns to track source list and contrast
      top_5_ora$list_name <- list_name
      top_5_ora$contrast_name <- contrast_name
      
      # Append results to the final data frame
      enriched_go_results <- rbind(enriched_go_results, top_5_ora)
    }
  }
}

# Save results as a CSV file
write.csv(enriched_go_results, "2.FunctionalAnalysis/output/top_5_enriched_GO_terms.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

This will help to identify the contrast in the final results
Match the names in degs_unique_list_pos with the names inside annotated_lists[[list_name]], and extract $name from degs_unique_list_pos accordingly.
```{r}
#Adding $name from degs_unique_list_pos to degs_unique_list
names(annotated_lists)

unique(names(annotated_lists[[2]][[1]]))
#Check that the order in degs_unique_list_pos is the same as in annotated_lists
all.equal(names(annotated_lists[[1]]), names(degs_unique_list_pos))
all.equal(names(annotated_lists[[2]]), names(degs_unique_list_pos))

#For each contrast_name in annotated_lists[[list_name]], check if it exists in degs_unique_list_pos.
#If a match is found, extract $name from degs_unique_list_pos[[contrast_name]].
#Only apply this change to lists in annotated_lists that start with "degs_unique_list".

# Initialize an empty data frame to store results
enriched_go_results <- data.frame()

# Loop through each list in annotated_lists
for (list_name in names(annotated_lists)) {
  
  # Loop through each contrast in the list
  for (contrast_name in names(annotated_lists[[list_name]])) {
    
    # Initialize second contrast name as NA
    second_contrast_name <- NA
    
    # If the list name starts with "degs_unique_list" and contrast_name exists in degs_unique_list_pos, extract the name
    if (grepl("^degs_unique_list", list_name) && contrast_name %in% names(degs_unique_list_pos)) {
      if (!is.null(degs_unique_list_pos[[contrast_name]]$name)) {
        second_contrast_name <- paste(unique(degs_unique_list_pos[[contrast_name]]$name), collapse = ", ")
      }
    }
    
    # Get the annotated genes for the contrast
    test_genes_ann <- as.data.frame(annotated_lists[[list_name]][[contrast_name]])
    
    # Perform ORA
    ora_test <- enricher(
      gene = test_genes_ann$gene_name1, 
      universe = all_pv_genes_ann$gene_name1, 
      TERM2GENE = all_pv_genes_ann[, c("go_desc", "gene_name1")], 
      pAdjustMethod = "BH",
      pvalueCutoff = 0.1
    )
    
    # Check if enrichment results exist
    if (!is.null(ora_test) && nrow(as.data.frame(ora_test)) > 0) {
      
      # Convert ORA results to a data frame
      ora_df <- as.data.frame(ora_test)
      
      # Select top 5 enriched GO terms
      top_5_ora <- ora_df[order(ora_df$p.adjust), ][1:min(5, nrow(ora_df)), ]
      
      # Replace "/" with "," in geneID
      top_5_ora$geneID <- gsub("/", ",", top_5_ora$geneID)
      
      # Add columns to track source list and contrast
      top_5_ora$list_name <- list_name
      
      # Append second contrast name only if it was found
      if (!is.na(second_contrast_name)) {
        top_5_ora$contrast_name <- paste(contrast_name, second_contrast_name, sep = " | ")
      } else {
        top_5_ora$contrast_name <- contrast_name
      }
      
      # Append results to the final data frame
      enriched_go_results <- rbind(enriched_go_results, top_5_ora)
    }
  }
}

# Save results as a CSV file
write.csv(enriched_go_results, "2.FunctionalAnalysis/output/top_5_enriched_GO_terms_contrastname.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

# Filter, classify, and plot Red Hawk vs Stampede upregulated genes under the "ADP binding" GO category by combined domain type (e.g., NB_LRR) 
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)


# --- Define tissue info ---
root_tissue_labels_abrev <- c("HYP", "RCR", "MBZ", "YBZ", 
                              "AUZT", "AUZB", "RTT", "RTB")

# --- 1. Read data ---
go_data <- read_tsv("2.FunctionalAnalysis/output/top5GO_genes_anngokeggpath_ord.tsv")

# --- 2. Filter by contrast and GO term ---
go_adp_redhawk_stampede <- go_data %>%
  filter(str_detect(contrast_name, "RedHawk_vs_Stampede")) %>%
  filter(go_desc == "ADP binding") %>%
  filter(list_name %in% c("de_upregulated_list", "de_downregulated_list"))

# --- 3. Tissue abbreviations ---
go_adp_redhawk_stampede <- go_adp_redhawk_stampede %>%
  mutate(
    tissue_full = str_extract(contrast_name, "^[^_]+"),
    tissue_abbrev = case_when(
      tissue_full == "Hypocotyl" ~ "HYP",
      tissue_full == "RootCrown" ~ "RCR",
      tissue_full == "MatureBranchedZoneTaproot" ~ "MBZ",
      tissue_full == "YoungBranchedZoneTaproot" ~ "YBZ",
      tissue_full == "AUZTaproot" ~ "AUZT",
      tissue_full == "AUZBasalRoots" ~ "AUZB",
      tissue_full == "RootTipTaproot" ~ "RTT",
      tissue_full == "RootTipBasalRoots" ~ "RTB",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    ),
    tissue_abbrev = factor(tissue_abbrev, levels = root_tissue_labels_abrev)
  )

# --- 4. Clean and summarize gene descriptions (abbreviating LRR) ---
gene_descriptions <- go_adp_redhawk_stampede %>%
  select(gene_name1, gene_description) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  mutate(
    gene_description_clean = str_replace_all(
      gene_description,
      regex("leucine[- ]rich repeat|LRR|leucine rich repeat", ignore_case = TRUE),
      "LRR"
    ),
    cnl_flag = str_detect(gene_description, regex("disease resistance protein", ignore_case = TRUE))
  ) %>%
  group_by(gene_name1) %>%
  summarise(
    gene_description_concat = paste(unique(gene_description_clean), collapse = " | "),
    lrr_in_description = any(str_detect(gene_description_clean, "LRR")),
    cnl_flag = any(cnl_flag),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# --- 5. Combine domain annotations per gene, sorted with NB-ARC first ---
gene_domains <- go_adp_redhawk_stampede %>%
  select(gene_name1, pfam_desc) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  mutate(pfam_desc = ifelse(pfam_desc == "NB-ARC", paste0("0_", pfam_desc), pfam_desc)) %>%
  group_by(gene_name1) %>%
  summarise(combined_domain = paste(sort(unique(pfam_desc)), collapse = "_"), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(combined_domain = str_replace_all(combined_domain, "0_", ""))

# --- 6. Join data and define regulation + updated NLR class including CNL ---
go_adp_domains <- go_adp_redhawk_stampede %>%
  left_join(gene_domains, by = "gene_name1") %>%
  left_join(gene_descriptions, by = "gene_name1") %>%
  mutate(
    regulation = case_when(
      list_name == "de_upregulated_list" ~ "Up in Stampede",
      list_name == "de_downregulated_list" ~ "Up in Red Hawk"
    ),
    nlr_class = case_when(
      str_detect(combined_domain, "NB-ARC") & str_detect(combined_domain, "Rx_N") ~ "CNL",
      str_detect(combined_domain, "NB-ARC") & cnl_flag ~ "CNL",
      str_detect(combined_domain, "NB-ARC") & str_detect(combined_domain, "TIR") ~ "TNL",
      str_detect(combined_domain, "NB-ARC") & str_detect(combined_domain, "RPW8") ~ "RNL",
      str_detect(combined_domain, "NB-ARC") & str_detect(combined_domain, "LRR") & !str_detect(combined_domain, "TIR|RPW8|Rx_N") ~ "NLR",
      str_detect(combined_domain, "NB-ARC") & !str_detect(combined_domain, "TIR|RPW8|LRR|Rx_N") & lrr_in_description ~ "NLR",
      str_detect(combined_domain, "NB-ARC") & !str_detect(combined_domain, "TIR|RPW8|LRR|Rx_N") ~ "NL",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    )
  )

# Define desired NLR class order
nlr_levels <- c("NL", "NLR", "CNL", "RNL", "TNL")

# Set factor levels in data
go_adp_domains <- go_adp_domains %>%
  mutate(nlr_class = factor(nlr_class, levels = nlr_levels))

#Save go_adp_domains for further analysis
#write.csv(go_adp_domains, "2.FunctionalAnalysis/output/go_adp_domains.csv")

# --- 7. Summarize counts ---
domain_summary <- go_adp_domains %>%
  select(gene_name1, nlr_class, regulation, tissue_abbrev) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  count(tissue_abbrev, nlr_class, regulation)

# --- 8. Color palette for NLR class (distinct from tissues) ---
nlr_colors <- c(
  "TNL" = "#ff5252",
  "NLR" = "#2c2c54",
  "NL"  = "#474787",
  "RNL" = "#cd6133",
  "Other" = "#b2df8a"
)

# Shared y-limit
max_count <- max(domain_summary$n)

# Common theme
plot_theme <- theme_classic(base_size = 16) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5)
  )

# --- Plot: Up in Stampede ---
plot_up_st <- ggplot(
  domain_summary %>% filter(regulation == "Up in Stampede"),
  aes(x = tissue_abbrev, y = n, fill = nlr_class)
) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  #geom_text(aes(label = n), vjust = -0.3, size = 4) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, max_count + 2)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = nlr_colors) +
  labs(
    x = "Tissue",
    y = "Gene Count",
    fill = "Class"
  ) +
  plot_theme

# --- Plot: Up in Red Hawk ---
plot_up_rh <- ggplot(
  domain_summary %>% filter(regulation == "Up in Red Hawk"),
  aes(x = tissue_abbrev, y = n, fill = nlr_class)
) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  #geom_text(aes(label = n), vjust = -0.3, size = 4) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, max_count + 2)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = nlr_colors) +
  labs(
    x = "Tissue",
    y = "Gene Count",
    fill = "Class"
  ) +
  plot_theme


# --- 11. Print & Save ---
print(plot_up_st)
print(plot_up_rh)

# --- Combine plots side-by-side ---
combined_plot <- plot_up_st + plot_up_rh +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect") & theme(legend.position = "bottom")

# --- Show combined plot ---
print(combined_plot)

# --- Save combined plot ---
ggsave("2.FunctionalAnalysis/figures/domain_ADPbinding_combined_NLRclasses_sm.pdf",
       plot = combined_plot,
       dpi = 600, width = 8.5, height = 3, units = "in")


# --- 11. Print & Save ---
print(plot_up_st)
print(plot_up_rh)

ggsave(plot = plot_up_st,
       filename = "2.FunctionalAnalysis/figures/domain_summary_ADPbinding_UpSt_NLRclass.pdf",
       dpi = 600, units = "in", height = 3, width = 4.5)

ggsave(plot = plot_up_rh,
       filename = "2.FunctionalAnalysis/figures/domain_summary_ADPbinding_UpRh_NLRclass.pdf",
       dpi = 600, units = "in", height = 3, width = 4)
```

# Compare GO for multiple gene lists for DEGs between genotypes, days and tissues using compareCluster

## Between genotypes
```{r}
#

#1. Subset the first 11 contrasts from each list
# Keep only the first 11 elements (your target tissues/days)
st_list <- annotated_lists[[3]][1:11]  # Upregulated in Stampede
rh_list <- annotated_lists[[4]][1:11]  # Upregulated in Red Hawk

#2. Name the entries to reflect genotype
names(st_list) <- paste0("Stampede_", names(st_list))
names(rh_list) <- paste0("RedHawk_", names(rh_list))

#3. Combine and extract just the gene vectors
gene_lists_named <- c(st_list, rh_list)
gene_lists_named <- lapply(gene_lists_named, function(df) df$gene_name1)

#4. Run compareCluster() with enricher()
TERM2GENE <- all_pv_genes_ann_ontology[, c("go_desc", "gene_name1")]
colnames(TERM2GENE) <- c("GOterm", "gene")

library(clusterProfiler)

ck <- compareCluster(
  geneCluster = gene_lists_named,
  fun = "enricher",
  TERM2GENE = TERM2GENE,
  universe = all_pv_genes_ann_ontology$gene_name1,
  pvalueCutoff = 0.05,#0.1
  pAdjustMethod = "BH"
)

#5. Add metadata (genotype, tissue, day) for plotting
res <- ck@compareClusterResult

res$genotype <- ifelse(grepl("^Stampede_", res$Cluster), "Stampede", "RedHawk")
res$day <- sub(".*_day([25])_.*", "Day \\1", res$Cluster)
```

# Expression (normalized gene counts) for enriched genes in GO terms
From script: 1_RDGA_Alltissues_nfstarsalmon.Rmd
Variance stabilization of counts
This step here is to visualize the variance stabilization step and to make PCA plot with stabilized counts. 
Normalization is automatically performed by DESeq2 when running the DESeq() function.

 Note, as suggested in the DESeq2 vignette: 
 - I used raw counts as input to DESeq() for differential expression analysis. 
   DESeq2 handles normalization and modeling internally to calculate log2 fold changes.
 - For visualizations (e.g., PCA, clustering, boxplots), I used VST counts 
   to stabilize variance and enable meaningful sample comparisons.
   

From DESeq2 vignette:
https://bioconductor.riken.jp/packages/3.17/bioc/vignettes/DESeq2/inst/doc/DESeq2.html
about vst: In all cases, the transformation is scaled such that for large counts, it becomes asymptotically (for
large values) equal to the logarithm to base 2 of normalized counts.

Maybe the most obvious choice of transformation is the logarithm. Since count values for a gene can be zero in some conditions (and non-zero in others), some advocate the use of pseudocounts, i.e. transformations of the form:

𝑦=log2(𝑛+𝑛0)

where n represents the count values and 𝑛0 is a positive constant.

In this section, we discuss two alternative approaches that offer more theoretical justification and a rational way of choosing parameters equivalent to 𝑛0 above. 
One makes use of the concept of variance stabilizing transformations (VST) (Tibshirani 1988; Huber et al. 2003; Anders and Huber 2010), and the other is the regularized logarithm or rlog, 
which incorporates a prior on the sample differences (Love, Huber, and Anders 2014). 
Both transformations produce transformed data on the log2 scale which has been normalized with respect to library size or other normalization factors.


```{r}  
#only roots ids
root_ids <- sampledata %>% 
  filter(!Tissue == "Leaf") %>% 
  pull(sample)

#This is using vst-transformed counts, note range of values 
#Filter t_variance_stabilised_counts to only roots
t_variance_stabilised_counts_roots <- t_variance_stabilised_counts[root_ids,]
dim(t_variance_stabilised_counts_roots)
range(t_variance_stabilised_counts_roots) #1.165345 14.649631
t_variance_stabilised_counts_roots[1:5,1:3]


library(DESeq2)
dds_roots_norm <- vst(dds_roots)

# Retrieve the normalized data from the `DESeqDataSet`
normalized_counts_roots <- assay(dds_roots_norm) %>%
  t() # Transpose this data

normalized_counts_roots[1:5,1:3]
dim(normalized_counts_roots)
range(normalized_counts_roots)#2.673161 14.663412

#Log2 transformation option, range is similar to variance stabilized counts
#These values are not affected by the DESeq contrast and reflect library-size 
#normalized expression for each gene across all samples.

# Extract normalized counts
deseqnorm_counts_roots <- counts(dds_roots, normalized = TRUE)
# Check the range of the normalized counts
range(deseqnorm_counts_roots) #0.00 25936.61
# Log2 transformation
log2norm_counts_roots <- log2(deseqnorm_counts_roots + 1)
# Check the range of the log2-transformed counts  
range(log2norm_counts_roots) #0.00000 14.66276
```

```{r}
# Make sure gene_id is a factor
my_AUZTd2UpSt_genes <- my_AUZTd2UpSt_genes %>%

my_AUZTd2UpRh_genes <- my_AUZTd2UpRh_genes %>%

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
#St
# Ensure gene_id is a factor
my_AUZTd2UpSt_genes <- my_AUZTd2UpSt_genes %>%
  mutate(gene_id = factor(gene_id))

# Get all unique Tissue-Day combinations
combos <- my_AUZTd2UpSt_genes %>%
  distinct(Tissue, Day)


#Rh
# Ensure gene_id is a factor
my_AUZTd2UpRh_genes <- my_AUZTd2UpRh_genes %>%
  mutate(gene_id = factor(gene_id))

# Get all unique Tissue-Day combinations
combos <- my_AUZTd2UpRh_genes %>%
  distinct(Tissue, Day)


plot_list <- list()
sig_table_list <- list()

# Loop over each Tissue + Day
for (i in 1:nrow(combos)) {
  
  tissue_name <- combos$Tissue[i]
  day_value <- combos$Day[i]
  
  df_subset <- my_AUZTd2UpRh_genes %>%
    filter(Tissue == tissue_name, Day == day_value) %>%
    mutate(
      gene_id = factor(gene_id),
      gene_num = as.numeric(gene_id)
    )
  
  gene_positions <- df_subset %>%
    select(gene_id) %>%
    distinct() %>%
    mutate(gene_num = as.numeric(gene_id))
  
  # Run t-tests and collect p-values (NO plotting)
  test_results <- df_subset %>%
    group_by(gene_id) %>%
    summarise(
      p = tryCatch(
        t.test(value ~ Genotype)$p.value,
        error = function(e) NA_real_
      ),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      p.adj = p.adjust(p, method = "fdr"),
      Tissue = tissue_name,
      Day = day_value
    )
  
  # Save the significance table
  sig_key <- paste(tissue_name, day_value, sep = "_")
  sig_table_list[[sig_key]] <- test_results
  
  # Build the plot (without geom_signif)
  # compare_means(value ~ Genotype, data = df_subset, 
  #             group.by = "gene_id", method = "t.test")
  p <- ggplot(df_subset, aes(x = gene_num, y = value)) +
    geom_jitter(aes(color = Genotype),
                position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.2, dodge.width = 0.8),
                size = 1, alpha = 0.4, show.legend = FALSE) +
    stat_summary(fun.data = mean_sdl, fun.args = list(mult = 1),
                 geom = "pointrange",
                 position = position_dodge(0.8),
                 aes(color = Genotype)) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("RedHawk" = "brown4", "Stampede" = "burlywood")) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("RedHawk" = "brown4", "Stampede" = "burlywood")) +
    scale_x_continuous(
      breaks = gene_positions$gene_num,
      labels = gene_positions$gene_id
    ) +
    theme_classic() +
    labs(
      title = paste("Tissue:", tissue_name, "| Day:", day_value),
      x = "Gene ID") +
      ylab(expression("VST-normalized gene counts (log"[2]*") scale")) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
  #p + stat_compare_means(aes(group = Genotype),
   #                      label = "p.signif",
                        #  method = "t.test",
                        #  comparisons = list(c("RedHawk", "Stampede")),
                        #  hide.ns = TRUE,
                        #  size = 3) +
   #stat_compare_means(label.y = 10.5, size = 3)
  plot_list[[sig_key]] <- p
}
```

## Violin plot
```{r }
library(ggpubr)

GENE_tissue_plot <- my_AUZTd2UpSt_genes %>% 
  filter(Day == "day2" | Day == "day5") %>%
  mutate(order_x = case_when(
    str_detect(Tissue, "Hypocotyl") ~ 1,
    str_detect(Tissue, "RootCrown") ~ 2,
    str_detect(Tissue, "MatureBranchedZoneTaproot") ~ 3,
    str_detect(Tissue, "YoungBranchedZoneTaproot") ~ 4,
    str_detect(Tissue, "AUZTaproot") ~ 5,
    str_detect(Tissue, "AUZBasalRoots") ~ 6,
    str_detect(Tissue, "RootTipTaproot") ~ 7,
    str_detect(Tissue, "RootTipBasalRoots") ~ 8
  )) %>% 
  mutate(Tissue = reorder(Tissue, order_x)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = Tissue, y = value, fill = Genotype)) +
  facet_grid(~Day, scales = "free_y") +
  
  # Violin plot
  geom_violin(aes(fill = Genotype, color = Genotype),
              position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), alpha = 0.5, trim = FALSE, color = NA,
              draw_quantiles = 0.5,  # Add median line
              linewidth = 0.5        # Outline thickness (optional)
              ) +
  
  # Dots inside violins
  geom_jitter(
    aes(color = Genotype),
    position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.2, dodge.width = 0.8),
    size = 0.8,
    alpha = 0.4,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  stat_summary(
  fun.data = median_hilow,
  fun.args = list(conf.int = 0.5),
  aes(group = Genotype, color = Genotype),
  geom = "crossbar",
  position = position_dodge(0.8),
  fill = NA
  #color = "black"  # or "white"
)+

  stat_compare_means(
  aes(x = Genotype, y = value),
  method = "t.test",
  comparisons = list(c("RedHawk", "Stampede")),
  label = "p.signif",
  inherit.aes = FALSE,
  data = my_AUZTd2UpSt_genes %>%
    filter(Day %in% c("day2", "day5")) %>%
    drop_na(value),  # Just in case!
  group.by = c("Tissue", "Day"),
  hide.ns = TRUE
)+

  scale_color_manual(values = c("RedHawk" = "brown4", "Stampede" = "burlywood")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("RedHawk" = "brown4", "Stampede" = "burlywood")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Normalized gene counts") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.spacing = unit(1, "lines"),
    text = element_text(size = 14),
    axis.text = element_text(color = "black"),
    axis.text.x = element_blank(),
    strip.background = element_blank()
  )

GENE_tissue <- wrap_plots(GENE_tissue_plot, module_lines_color_strip,
           nrow = 2, heights = c(1, 0.08))

GENE_tissue

# Save GENE_tissue plot in PDF
ggsave(plot = GENE_tissue, filename = "2.FunctionalAnalysis/figures/AUZTd2UpSt_box.pdf", dpi = 600, units = "in", height = 4, width = 7)
```

## Querying OrgDb for Phaseolus vulgaris with AnnotationHub
From:https://yulab-smu.top/biomedical-knowledge-mining-book/GOSemSim.html#gosemsim-supported-organisms 

We can query OrgDb online via the AnnotationHub package
```{r ora12}
library(AnnotationHub)
hub <- AnnotationHub()
q <- query(hub, "Phaseolus vulgaris")
q
id <- q$ah_id[length(q)]
Pvulgaris <- hub[[id]]
Pvulgaris

# Load required package
library(AnnotationDbi)

# See available key types (types of IDs you can extract)
keytypes(Pvulgaris)

# For example, list a few Gene IDs
gene_ids <- head(keys(Pvulgaris, keytype = "GID"))
print(gene_ids)

# If you want to see the SYMBOLs (gene names) or other info associated with those Gene IDs:
select(Pvulgaris, keys = gene_ids, columns = c("SYMBOL", "GENENAME"), keytype = "GID")

```

I'm not sure if this OrgDb is the genome version 2.1. There is "BSCHEMAVERSION: 2.1" but I don't know if this refers to the genome version.
If this is the genome version, I could use it for future analysis that require an OrgDb.
